Danish Meteorological Institute.fact: A dual Cray XT5 marked the switch from vector to scalar in 2007. From 2016, the Icelandic Meteorological Office (Veðurstofa) manages a 192 teraFLOPS dual Cray XC30 system for DMI as weather forecast, due to cheaper electricity and cooling.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The _____ was Rapid climate fluctuation in the last glacial period.
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: A Dansgaard–Oeschger event (often abbreviated D–O event) is a rapid climate fluctuation; such events occurred 25 times during the last glacial period.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The comparable climate cyclicity during the _____ is referred to as Bond events
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The comparable climate cyclicity during the Holocene is called Bond events.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: If this relationship holds also for the previous glacials, _____ data suggest that D-O events were present in previous glacial periods as well
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: Ice core evidence from Antarctic cores suggests that the Dansgaard–Oeschger events are related to the so-called Antarctic Isotope Maxima by means of a coupling of the climate of the two hemispheres, the polar see-saw. If this relationship holds also for the previous glacials, Antarctic data suggest that D-O events were present in previous glacial periods as well.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: However, work by _____ and colleagues has shown that the existing Greenland record can be reconstructed by deriving the Antarctic ice core record
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: However, work by Stephen Barker and colleagues has shown that the existing Greenland record can be reconstructed by deriving the Antarctic ice core record.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This allows for the reconstruction of an older _____ record through the derivation of the nearly million-year-long Antarctic ice core record
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: Unfortunately, current ice core records from Greenland extend only through the last most recent glacial period so direct evidence of D-O events in earlier glacial periods from Greenland ice is unavailable. However, work by Stephen Barker and colleagues has shown that the existing Greenland record can be reconstructed by deriving the Antarctic ice core record.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The impact of D-O events in _____ is also recorded by fluctuations in discharge and sedimentation patterns in fluvial systems like the Tisza River
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The impact of D-O events in Europe is also recorded by fluctuations in discharge and sedimentation patterns in fluvial systems like the Tisza River.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This cold period sees an expansion of the polar front, with ice floating further south across the _____
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: This cold period sees an expansion of the polar front, with ice floating further south across the North Atlantic Ocean.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: During D-O events, positive δ18O excursions occur in _____ speleothem records, indicating a weakening of the Indonesian-Australian Monsoon during such events
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: During D-O events, positive δ18O excursions occur in Floresian speleothem records, indicating a weakening of the Indonesian-Australian Monsoon during such events.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The effects of D-O events have also been observed in the _____, where D-O events during the Penultimate Glacial Period have been shown to have corresponded to changes in vegetation regimes
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The effects of D-O events have also been observed in the Northern Andes, where D-O events during the Penultimate Glacial Period have been shown to have corresponded to changes in vegetation regimes.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The pattern in the _____ is different, with slow warming and much smaller temperature fluctuations
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The pattern in the Southern Hemisphere is different, with slow warming and much smaller temperature fluctuations.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The events appear to reflect changes in the _____ circulation, perhaps triggered by an influx of fresh water or rain
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The events appear to reflect changes in the North Atlantic Ocean circulation, perhaps triggered by an influx of fresh water or rain.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The former determines the strength of the _____ circulation via altering the northern hemisphere westerly winds, gulf stream, and sea-ice systems
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The events appear to reflect changes in the North Atlantic Ocean circulation, perhaps triggered by an influx of fresh water or rain. The former determines the strength of the Atlantic Ocean circulation via altering the northern hemisphere westerly winds, gulf stream, and sea-ice systems.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The latter modulates atmospheric inter-basin freshwater transport across _____, which changes the freshwater budget in the North Atlantic and thus the circulation
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The latter modulates atmospheric inter-basin freshwater transport across Central America, which changes the freshwater budget in the North Atlantic and thus the circulation.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: A spectral analysis of the American GISP2 isotope record showed a peak of [18O:16O] abundance around _____ years
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: A spectral analysis of the American GISP2 isotope record showed a peak of [18O:16O] abundance around 1500 years.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This was proposed by Schulz (_____) to be a regular periodicity of 1470 years
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: This was proposed by Schulz (2002) to be a regular periodicity of 1470 years.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This finding was supported by Rahmstorf (_____); if only the most recent 50,000 years from the GISP2 core are examined, the variation of the trigger is ±12% (±2% in the 5 most recent events, whose dat
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: This finding was supported by Rahmstorf (2003); if only the most recent 50,000 years from the GISP2 core are examined, the variation of the trigger is ±12% (±2% in the 5 most recent events, whose dates are probably most precise).

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: However, the older parts of the GISP2 core do not show this regularity, nor do the same events in the _____ core
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: However, the older parts of the GISP2 core do not show this regularity, nor do the same events in the GRIP core.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: Oscillations within the _____ system can be expected to be far more irregular in period
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: Oscillations within the Earth system can be expected to be far more irregular in period.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The closest orbital cycle, a _____ cycle of 1,800 years, cannot be reconciled with this pattern
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The closest orbital cycle, a Lunar cycle of 1,800 years, cannot be reconciled with this pattern.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The dating between the _____ GRIP ice core, and the American GISP2 ice core differs by about 5000 years at 50,000 years BP
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The dating between the European GRIP ice core, and the American GISP2 ice core differs by about 5000 years at 50,000 years BP.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: It was noted by _____ et al
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: It was noted by Ditlevsen et al.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: (_____) that the spectral peak found in the GISP2 ice core was not present in the GRIP core, and thus depended critically on the accuracy of the dating
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: (2005) that the spectral peak found in the GISP2 ice core was not present in the GRIP core, and thus depended critically on the accuracy of the dating.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The dating issue was largely solved by the accurate dating of the _____ core
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The dating issue was largely solved by the accurate dating of the NGRIP core.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: (_____) suggested that each ice sheet had its own conditions of stability, but that on melting, the influx of freshwater was enough to reconfigure ocean currents, causing melting elsewhere
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: (2001) suggested that each ice sheet had its own conditions of stability, but that on melting, the influx of freshwater was enough to reconfigure ocean currents, causing melting elsewhere.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This warmer water results in melting of Antarctic ice, thereby reducing density stratification and the strength of the _____ current (AABW)
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: This warmer water results in melting of Antarctic ice, thereby reducing density stratification and the strength of the Antarctic Bottom Water current (AABW).

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This allows the NADW to return to its previous strength, driving _____ melting – and another D-O cold event
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: More specifically, D-O cold events, and their associated influx of meltwater, reduce the strength of the North Atlantic Deep Water current (NADW), weakening the northern hemisphere circulation and therefore resulting in an increased transfer of heat polewards in the southern hemisphere. This allows the NADW to return to its previous strength, driving Northern Hemisphere melting – and another D-O cold event.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: D-O events tend to be what drives the "_____ pump" which has had an effect upon human evolution and dispersal
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: D-O events tend to be what drives the "Sahara pump" which has had an effect upon human evolution and dispersal.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The cyclicity is also found during the _____, where the events are referred to as Bond events
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The cyclicity is also found during the Holocene, where the events are called Bond events.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: This may be because the first _____ kyr of the GISP2 core are most accurately dated, by layer counting
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: This finding was supported by Rahmstorf (2003); if only the most recent 50,000 years from the GISP2 core are examined, the variation of the trigger is ±12% (±2% in the 5 most recent events, whose dates are probably most precise). This may be because the first 50 kyr of the GISP2 core are most accurately dated, by layer counting.

Dansgaard–Oeschger event.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.question: The climate system response to the trigger is varying within _____ of the period
Dansgaard–Oeschger event.fact: The climate system response to the trigger is varying within 8% of the period.

DBFS.subject: Meteorology & Climate
DBFS.question: The _____ was Unit of measurement for amplitude levels in digital systems.
DBFS.fact: dBFS or dB FS (decibels relative to full scale) is a unit of measurement for amplitude levels in digital systems, such as pulse-code modulation (PCM), which have a defined maximum peak level. The level of 0 dBFS is assigned to the maximum possible digital level.

DBFS.subject: Meteorology & Climate
DBFS.question: dBFS is defined in AES Standard AES17-_____, IEC 61606, and ITU-T Recs
DBFS.fact: dBFS is defined in AES Standard AES17-1998, IEC 61606, and ITU-T Recs.

DBFS.subject: Meteorology & Climate

DBFS.fact: This convention is used in Wolfson and Cirrus Logic digital microphone specs, etc.

DBFS.question: The CD-DA Red Book (_____) standard defined the maximum loudness should be 0 dBFS
DBFS.fact: The CD-DA Red Book (1980) standard defined the maximum loudness should be 0 dBFS.

DBFS.fact: For example, a signal that reaches 50% of the maximum level has a level of −6 dBFS, which is 6 dB below full scale.

DBm.subject: Meteorology & Climate
DBm.question: The _____ was Power level referenced to one milliwatt.
DBm.fact: dBm or dBmW (decibel-milliwatts) is a unit of power level expressed using a logarithmic decibel (dB) scale respective to one milliwatt (mW).

DBm.question: dBW is a similar unit measured relative to one watt (_____ mW) rather than a milliwatt
DBm.fact: dBW is a similar unit measured relative to one watt (1000 mW) rather than a milliwatt.

DBm.fact: In United States Department of Defense practice, unweighted measurement is normally understood, applicable to a certain bandwidth, which must be stated or implied.

DBZ (meteorology).question: The _____ was Unit of measure used in weather radar.
DBZ (meteorology).fact: dBZ is a logarithmic dimensionless technical unit used in radar. It is mostly used in weather radar, to compare the equivalent reflectivity factor (Z) of a remote object (in mm6 per m3) to the return of a droplet of rain with a diameter of 1 mm (1 mm6 per m3).

Decibel.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Decibel.question: The _____ was Logarithmic unit expressing the ratio of physical quantities.
Decibel.fact: The decibel (symbol: dB) is a relative unit of measurement equal to one tenth of a bel (B). Two signals whose levels differ by one decibel have a power ratio of 101/10 (approximately 1.26) or root-power ratio of 101/20 (approximately 1.12).
